faq.q: Can I set a countdown to repeat?
faq.a: Yes. Each countdown has a Recurring setting — one-time, weekly, monthly or yearly. When a recurring target passes, it automatically rolls the date forward to the next occurrence (and resets its celebration), so a yearly birthday or New Year keeps counting to the next one without you re-entering it. Presets for New Year, birthday, Diwali, Holi and exams are built in.

faq.q: What happens when a countdown reaches zero?
faq.a: A confetti celebration animation plays. Cards for past events flip to counting up as 'time since'. The list sorts soonest-first with past events last. You can also set milestone alerts at 1 day, 1 hour or 10 minutes — but these use browser notifications and only fire while the tab stays open, which the tool states plainly.

faq.q: How do I move my countdowns to a real calendar?
faq.a: Use Export .ics to get a standard calendar file with every countdown as an event (recurring ones carry an RRULE), which you can import into Google, Apple or Outlook calendar. There's also Export JSON and a Backup ZIP (JSON + text summary + .ics + README). The deep notes stress that a calendar entry, not the tab-based countdown, is the reliable safeguard for a true deadline.

If you name a countdown like an exam, you can select it in the Study Planner and it splits the remaining days into a revision schedule: roughly 50% to learn new syllabus, 30% to revision and notes, 20% to mock tests and weak areas. It's labelled as guidance to adjust to your own syllabus. There's also a progress bar if you set an optional start date.
